correctness.rationale: Writing S for the squared Frobenius norm, sign averaging gives second moment S/n. In the fourth moment only a repeated cell and products of two disjoint cells survive, with probabilities 1/n and 1/[n(n-1)] and pair multinomial factor 6. For normalized squared masses, T is their squared sum, P the unordered colliding-pair sum and D the unordered disjoint-pair sum. Then T+2P+2D=1, so K=n-2nP+2n(4-n)D/(n-1). For n≥4 this gives the upper bound and isolates partial matchings at four and singletons above four. At n=2,3, repartitioning the total mass of two colliding positive cells gives a strictly convex one-variable objective (their joint term in D is absent), so a maximizer has matching support. On a matching K=3n/(n-1)+n(n-4)T/(n-1), maximized only when T=1/n, i.e. a full equal-mass matching. For the lower bound the variance of the squared linear form is the permutation variance of the selected squared-mass sum plus 4/[n(n-1)] times the unnormalized disjoint-pair sum. Zero of the latter forces a star; zero of the former then forces all n entries in that row/column to have a single positive absolute value. The interval follows by connectedness. For Banach–Mazur distance, averaging the two squared norm inequalities over signed row and column actions preserves them and turns any candidate quadratic form into a scalar Frobenius form, by sign elimination of off-diagonal terms and transitivity on entries. This proves optimal distortion with precisely the fourth root claimed. All steps use n≥2, real matrices, and independent fair signs.
residual_risks: No assertion for complex matrices, correlated signs or the index-two even-signed subgroup.
